title: Devin Anderson – Strategy versus Structure in Tail Hedging (S6E14)

reader_summary.overview: All opinions expressed by podcast participants are solely their own opinion. My guest this episode is Devin Anderson, co-founder of Convexitas. The theme of this episode, as you can likely guess from the title, is strategy versus structure.

key_points.text: While we often focus on strategy specifics on this podcast.
key_points.evidence_quote: While we often focus on strategy specifics on this podcast, Devin hosts a masterclass as to why the structure you wrap your strategy in can ultimately determine the type of strategy you can deliver.

key_points.text: Specifically, we discuss option-based tail hedging and the types of strategies that can be delivered in hedge fund, mutual fund, ETF.
key_points.evidence_quote: Specifically, we discuss option-based tail hedging and the types of strategies that can be delivered in hedge fund, mutual fund, ETF, and separate account wrappers.

key_points.text: In the back half of the conversation, we dive into how Convexitas implements their risk-mitigating strategies.
key_points.evidence_quote: In the back half of the conversation, we dive into how Convexitas implements their risk-mitigating strategies.

thesis: The episode argues that the structural wrapper of an investment product fundamentally determines the type of strategy it can deliver, specifically regarding option-based tail hedging. The host and guest explain that one cannot simultaneously achieve high scalability, tax efficiency, and investment flexibility, forcing managers to make tradeoffs between path dependency, tax treatment, and scalability when designing risk mitigation products.
